rationale: Correct the existing PROENERGY platform without duplicating ECP. Retain ECP Fund V as the current majority owner, add the disclosed management co-investment, preserve former ACON and Eos sponsor participation, and treat the 2025 and 2026 power-plant sales as asset-level partial realizations rather than a platform exit. PROENERGY Services, WattBridge, business segments and plants remain subordinate to the canonical company.

companyFieldUpdates.name: PROENERGY
companyFieldUpdates.description: PROENERGY is a Sedalia, Missouri-based power-infrastructure platform founded in 2002 that manufactures and packages aeroderivative generation equipment, executes turnkey projects, supplies contracted power and provides lifecycle services to utilities, municipalities, independent power producers and data-center customers. ECP Fund V completed a majority investment in August 2024 from affiliates of Eos Partners and ACON Investments; founder Jeff Canon and management invested alongside ECP. Exact sponsor and management percentages and the acquisition vehicle are not publicly disclosed. PROENERGY Services is an operating identity and WattBridge is a contracted-power subsidiary or segment rather than a separate PortCo. CPS Energy acquired four plants totaling 1,632 MW for US$1.387 billion in September 2025, and STEC acquired two plants totaling 768 MW for US$768 million in April 2026. Those transactions monetized assets while PROENERGY retained service relationships and did not sell the platform. ECP and Bridgepoint continue to report PROENERGY as current, and no later company sale or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.
